removability.rationale: The route itself deletes cleanly, but the feature leaks into the Pokémon page's data mapping and template, and ability-only concerns (hidden flag) are threaded through shared helpers and CSS, so removal leaves traces unless you hunt them.

evidence: app/app/utils/poke.ts:90 — spriteUrl is the single sprite-URL seam, used by every card list
app/app/utils/poke.ts:24-31 — humanize/englishName/latestEnglishFlavorText centralized, not re-implemented per page
app/app/pages/index.vue:104-109 — cardOf duplicates the card-model construction instead of reusing cardsFromPokemonRefs
app/app/utils/poke.ts:63-79 — API cache and failure handling in one function
changeability.rationale: Most fixes land in one obvious place (spriteUrl, humanize, the data layer), but home-page card construction is a parallel copy of the shared builder, so model changes can require two edits.

evidence: app/app/components/PokemonCard.vue:5-9 — depends only on a typed PokemonCardModel plus optional types prop
app/app/components/MovesTable.vue:7-10 — typed MoveRow[] prop; no knowledge of fetching or pages
app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:98 — whole typeEn map serialized into the page payload just for move rows, an awkward internal leak
app/app/pages/abilities/[name].vue:17 — hidden-ability lookup re-matches entries by ref.url in a callback (fragile O(n^2) matching)

coupling.rationale: Components consume narrow typed models and all state lives in the URL; the data layer is the only shared module. Only minor tangles: the typeEn map pushed through the payload and the url-matching callback.

evidence: app/app/utils/poke.ts:233-263 — cardsFromPokemonRefs is a real abstraction over refs→species variation (dedupe, forms, ordering)
app/app/pages/moves/[name].vue:36-37 — the fetchRecord→404→useHead page skeleton is copy-pasted in all four detail pages (also abilities:31-32, types:45-46, pokemon:172-173)
app/app/pages/types/[name].vue:71-76 — 'count + card grid' section markup duplicated in moves, abilities and types pages
app/app/components/MovesTable.vue — sorting variation properly encapsulated, no flag-parameter creep
abstraction_design.rationale: The card and move-table abstractions are well designed for the real variation, but the detail-page skeleton and card-grid section exist only as per-page copies, so a similar new section (Items) means duplicating a page file rather than reusing a composable.

findings.issue: The detail-page skeleton (useAsyncData + fetchRecord → null, computed useHead title, useRequestEvent 404) is duplicated verbatim across all four detail pages instead of a shared composable.
findings.suggestion: Extract a useResourcePage(key, resource, name) composable (or a small wrapper) that returns { data } and handles the head title and 404 status; new sections then reuse it.

findings.issue: cardOf re-implements the PokemonCardModel mapping (sprite, name, hidden) already centralized in cardsFromPokemonRefs, so card semantics live in two places.
findings.suggestion: Build home cards through a shared card-model builder (or have HomeSpecies carry the model) so card construction has one home in poke.ts.

findings.issue: The '<count> Pokémon' + card-grid section markup is triplicated across the moves, abilities and types pages.
findings.suggestion: Add a CardGrid (or 'PokemonSection') component taking cards + heading, and use it in all three pages plus the new home-page grid.

findings.issue: Ability-specific 'hidden' handling is threaded through the generic cardsFromPokemonRefs and PokemonCard, so removing/changing abilities touches shared code.
findings.suggestion: Keep the hidden marker out of the shared model; let the ability page pass a slot or a per-list badge so the concern stays in the abilities feature.

findings.issue: The API base default literal ('http://localhost:9000') is duplicated in nuxt.config.ts and poke.ts:54; changing the default needs two edits.
findings.suggestion: Let runtimeConfig own the default and have poke.ts start from a placeholder that setApiBase always overwrites (the plugin already guarantees it runs first).

findings.issue: The entire type-name→English map is serialized into the page payload (typeEn) just to label move-table rows, enlarging the client payload and coupling the move model to the full type index.
findings.suggestion: Resolve typeEn inside the moves useAsyncData against getTypeIndex(), keeping the map server-side.

findings.issue: Hidden-ability detection re-finds the matching entry by comparing ref.url inside a callback per card — fragile and O(n²).
findings.suggestion: Map entries to { ref, isHidden } pairs first, then call cardsFromPokemonRefs once over the flattened list.

findings.issue: Build artifacts (.nuxt/, .output/, .data/) sit inside app/ with no .gitignore entry covering them (root .gitignore ignores only /data/, /.data-cache/, node_modules/), so builds dirty the repo.
findings.suggestion: Add app/.nuxt, app/.output and app/.data to .gitignore.

summary: A tidy, idiomatic Nuxt 4 app (pinned to the current stable 4.6.3) with a single well-factored data layer, typed component seams and URL-driven state, so most fixes land in one obvious place. Its editability ceiling is page-level copy-paste: the detail-page skeleton, card construction and card-grid markup are duplicated per page instead of extracted, which is exactly what a new Items-like section would feel. I'd merge this and ask for a follow-up extracting a page composable and a card-grid component.
